source_title: DCN Dx Acquires Human Biospecimen Provider BioSouthTech to Broaden Access to Diverse Patient Populations - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
Latin American collection network and banked specimens support broader patient representation and earlier-stage cancer research
CARLSBAD, Calif. , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DCN Dx today announced its acquisition of BioSouthTech, Inc., a human biospecimen provider headquartered in the Miami area, with a collection network across Latin America, including South America, and access to specimens from the Caribbean. The acquisition expands DCN Dx's sample bank and patient access for drug and diagnostic research.
Access to a broader range of patient specimens helps diagnostic developers study how their tests perform across different populations. BioSouthTech expands that access through its banked specimens and Latin American collection network.
"We started our biospecimens business to give researchers better access to patients and support the collections their studies require," said Charlie Mamrak, CEO of DCN Dx. "Patient diversity was central to that decision. BioSouthTech gives our customers more ways to reach populations that their existing specimen sources may not represent."
For developers of liquid biopsy assays, including multi-cancer early detection (MCED) and measurable residual disease (MRD) tests, specimens must reflect the disease stages and patient populations under study. The acquisition broadens DCN Dx's sourcing options for oncology, neurology, and autoimmune disease research.
"You can't develop a test for everyone on data from a few," said Jim Boushell, senior vice president of biospecimens at DCN Dx. "For two decades, I've watched technology evolve on data that doesn't quite reflect the patients those tests are meant to serve. We pursued BioSouthTech to give developers access to more diverse patient populations, including treatment-naive patients. Patient diversity must be part of the evidence."
Starting now, DCN Dx customers can request characterized tissue and matched sets off the shelf or stand-up prospective collections designed to their own protocol across oncology, neurology, and infectious disease. The network already reaches patients across a range of ancestries and regions, and new geographies and expanded cohorts are planned for early 2027.
For more information about DCN Dx's biospecimen services, visit dcndx.com/services/biospecimen .
For more than 20 years, DCN Dx has helped companies bring diagnostic tests to commercial success. The company combines an immunoassay CDMO, an IVD-dedicated CRO, and a biospecimen business offering banked specimens and direct collections. Its biospecimen team connects developers with diverse patient populations and specimens aligned to their study protocols and intended use. Direct collections operate under IRB/IEC oversight, with standardized protocols, clinical and demographic data, and chain-of-custody documentation. DCN Dx is based in Carlsbad, California. Learn more at dcndx.com .
